name: Doro Wat
ingredients: 1/2 cup niter kibbeh (spiced butter) or oil
instructions: Cook the onions slowly in a dry pot, stirring often, until deeply softened.
Stir in the niter kibbeh, then the berbere, garlic and ginger; cook a few minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken pieces and enough water to just cover; simmer, covered, until the chicken is tender.
Nestle in the boiled eggs for the last 10 minutes so they soak up the sauce.
Finish with lemon juice and serve hot with injera.

name: Kitfo
instructions: Warm the niter kibbeh gently until just melted, not hot.
Mix the mitmita and garlic into the warm butter.
Fold the seasoned butter through the minced beef until evenly coated.
Serve immediately, mounded on a plate with ayib and gomen alongside.

name: Tibs
ingredients: 500g beef or lamb, cut into cubes
instructions: Sear the meat in hot oil in a wide pan until browned on all sides.
Add the onions and pepper, and cook until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary and berbere; cook a few more minutes.
Serve sizzling, straight from the pan, with injera or bread.

name: Shiro Wat
instructions: Soften the onion in oil, then add garlic and tomato and cook down.
Whisk the shiro powder into water until smooth and lump-free.
Pour into the pan, stirring constantly as it thickens.
Simmer gently for 10 minutes, adding water if it gets too thick, then serve.

name: Misir Wat
instructions: Cook the onion in oil until golden, then add garlic, ginger and berbere.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for a minute.
Add the lentils and water; bring to a boil, then simmer, stirring occasionally.
Cook until the lentils break down into a thick stew, about 20 minutes.

name: Gomen
ingredients: 1 large bunch collard greens, finely shredded
instructions: Soften the onion in oil, then add garlic and ginger.
Add the shredded greens in batches, stirring until wilted.
Cover and cook on low heat until tender, about 15 minutes.
Season to taste and serve warm.

name: Atkilt Wat
instructions: Soften the onion in oil, then stir in turmeric.
Add potatoes and carrots first, since they take longest to cook.
Add the cabbage once the potatoes are almost tender.
Cover and cook until all the vegetables are soft, stirring occasionally.

name: Injera
ingredients: 5 cups water, plus more to thin
A splash of starter batter from a previous ferment (optional, speeds things up)
instructions: Whisk the teff flour and water into a smooth, thin batter.
Cover loosely and leave at room temperature for 2-3 days to ferment until bubbly and sour.
Thin the batter with water to a pourable consistency just before cooking.
Pour in a thin spiral onto a hot, lightly oiled flat pan, cover, and steam-cook until the surface is full of small holes and set.

name: Ambasha
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and a pinch of the sugar in the warm water; let it foam.
Mix the flour, remaining sugar and cardamom, then work in the oil and yeast mixture.
Knead until smooth, then let rise, covered, until doubled.
Shape into a round loaf, score a decorative pattern on top, and bake until golden.

name: Buna (Coffee Ceremony)
instructions: Wash the green beans, then roast them in a pan over heat, stirring constantly until dark and fragrant.
Let the beans cool slightly, then grind them coarsely.
Brew the grounds with water in a jebena (clay coffee pot) over heat until it comes to a boil.
Pour slowly into small cups, leaving the grounds behind, and serve with popcorn.

name: Dabo Kolo
ingredients: 1/2 tsp berbere (optional, for a spiced version)
instructions: Mix the flour, oil, sugar and berbere, then bring together with a little water into a stiff dough.
Roll into thin ropes and cut into small bite-sized pieces.
Fry in batches until golden and crisp, or bake at a moderate oven temperature, turning once.
Cool completely before serving or storing in an airtight container.
